positioning: For Goodnotes users on an iPad who want one calm everyday planner they can start the week they buy it, in any month, and never have to replace when the year rolls over: an undated portrait planner whose pages fill the iPad screen, opens in the first five minutes (Start here plus a Setup check page), and keeps every page two taps away. It wins against the 600-page dated bundles on the things their buyers complain about most: downloads and setup, apps and screen fit, and getting lost.

must_haves.what: One portrait PDF made for Goodnotes first (named first in the title, the listing and the Start here page), that also opens in Notability, Noteshelf, Samsung Notes and Xodo. Plain PDF links only, no app-specific tricks.

Works for any year and any start day: 12 undated month pages, 52 week pages numbered from the week the buyer starts (not tied to fixed months) and 364 day pages. The buyer writes the dates; nothing expires on December 31.

Hyperlinked everywhere: Contents, Year, a Weeks page with all 52 weeks, month tabs down the right edge of every page, each week to its seven days, every day to the next and previous day (across week edges too), and a Weeks / Week trail at the top right of every week and day page.

The core set buyers use every day: year overview, 12 month pages with goals and notes, a habit tracker for every month, 52 week pages, a page for every day with top 3, to do, time blocks and notes, a Lists page and 6 notes pages.

A finished, quiet design with real typography: two font families only (Cormorant Garamond for headings and italic labels, Manrope for body text), consistent spacing, indigo and soft gold month tabs. Design is the biggest praise driver.
Instructions printed inside the file (Start here, Setup check, a how-the-links-work note on Contents), not only in a video or a separate PDF.

fixes.how: Ships as one PDF, not a zip, under 19.5 MB. The listing and photo 9 give the download in three steps: buy, download from Etsy in a web browser (the Etsy app cannot download digital files), open the PDF in Goodnotes with Share, then Open in Goodnotes, or in Goodnotes with New, then Import. The Start here page repeats the steps.

The cover's Open planner button lands on a 4-step Start here page (import it, check the links, start in the month you are in, pen off to tap and on to write) with a months grid underneath, so step 3 is one tap. The next page is a Setup check with buttons that jump and a pen test box. Nothing to assemble: there are no stickers, covers or add-on files to import.

Pages are 768 x 1024 portrait, the iPad's own 3:4 shape, so in Goodnotes the page fills the screen with no blank bands at the sides (the size complaint on a top seller's portrait planner). The listing has a Works with / Not for box: works in Goodnotes, Notability, Noteshelf, Samsung Notes and Xodo on iPad and Android tablets; not made for phones, e-ink tablets or for viewing in Files, Photos or a Google Drive preview. The Setup check page proves the links on the buyer's own device in one minute.

Every day page has the same five boxes in the same places (Top 3, To do, Notes on the left; Time blocks 6am to 9pm and Good things today on the right), and every week page is the same two columns of day boxes, so there is one layout to learn. Home, Year, Lists and Notes sit on the top bar of every page.

Month tabs run down the right edge of every page; Weeks on the top bar opens a page with all 52 weeks; each week links its seven days; day pages have large previous and next buttons that also cross from Sunday to the next Monday; every week and day page has a Weeks / Week trail. Weeks run 1 to 52 in order from the buyer's first week, so the next-week button always opens the following week.

Every listing photo is a screenshot of the built file, captioned with the page name; no mockup shows anything the file lacks. The description lists each page type with counts and says plainly: undated (you write the dates), portrait only, Monday-start weeks, no stickers, handwrite or use the app's text tool (not a fillable form), English only.

The Setup check page turns 'it doesn't work' into a 30-second test: three buttons that must jump, and a four-line Nothing happened? list (pen off, open it in a planner app not Files, re-import the PDF, then send the shop an Etsy message). The build checks every link resolves and every page is reachable from the cover.

Most support messages are setup questions, so the answers are in the file and the listing: the Setup check fix list, the Start here steps and a listing FAQ with the top five problems (Etsy app download, which app, links not tapping because the pen is on, how to type, how undated weeks work). The listing says what the buyer can do (Setup check, then send the shop an Etsy message) and promises no reply time.

Undated, so it fits the buyer's calendar: start any day and keep going for 52 weeks. Photos 2 to 4 show the day, week and month pages close up and readable, and the listing lists what is not inside (no budget, meal or fitness sections), so buyers who need those do not buy the wrong planner.

One purchase covers 52 weeks from whenever the buyer starts and never goes out of date. Writing room is generous: half of each day page is time blocks and open writing, each weekday has its own tall lined box on the week page, text is set at 1.1 scale. Photo 2 shows the day page close up at about twice its on-screen size.

unique.name: Start any day, weeks that follow you
unique.what: Weeks 1 to 52 run in order from the week the buyer starts, on any day of the year, instead of being tied to fixed months; a Weeks page lists all 52 with a line to write each first date. Start here says: open Week 1, write this Monday's date, start on today. Undated month pages have 6-row grids (42 boxes), so every real month fits.
unique.why: Buyers ask for next year's edition and complain about months with missing date boxes; an undated planner that fits every month removes both, and lets an October or mid-year buyer start today.

unique.name: Portrait pages that fill the iPad
unique.what: Every page is 768 x 1024, exactly the iPad's 3:4 portrait shape, with week pages laid out as two tall columns of day boxes (Monday to Thursday, Friday to Sunday and Notes) and the week's top 3 and notes underneath.
unique.why: Only 10% of top sellers offer portrait and a top portrait seller is criticised for blank space at the sides in Goodnotes; screen fit is part of the device complaints.

unique.name: Setup check page
unique.what: A page with buttons that jump to a month, the year and Contents, a pen test box, a fix list for when nothing happens, and a map of what each top-bar button opens.
unique.why: Download, setup and 'doesn't work' are three of the four biggest complaint clusters; no top seller shows a test page.

unique.name: Time blocks on every day
unique.what: Each day page has hourly time blocks from 6am to 9pm beside a Top 3 list, so the day is planned by time, not only as a to-do list.
unique.why: No top seller shows time blocking in their titles; planning by the hour is the daily habit buyers praise.

waived.reason: Deliberately undated: undated listings hold 63% of all-time sales among top sellers and our dated Goodnotes planner (Just Today, p-adhd-001) already covers the dated 2027 buyer. The listing says undated in the title.

look.direction: Quiet ink and indigo on warm ivory with soft gold accents, portrait, lots of air. Headings in Cormorant Garamond, labels in its italic, body in Manrope: two families, hierarchy from weight, size and italic. Month tabs run from indigo to soft gold. High contrast ink (#1E2238 on #FBF9F4) for low-light reading; no tracked all-caps labels.
avoid: Pastel rainbow tabs and sticker-heavy covers
Sage green and teal (our Just Today planner)

price.why: At the bottom of the best-earning band ($28 to $52) and above what buyers actually pay weighted by sales ($25.66). It replaces a yearly dated planner, so it is priced as a full planner, not a $4 template. While the shop has few reviews it launches with a 30-day 25% Etsy sale on the full price instead of a low price (style rule r015).

Open it in Goodnotes or another planner app, not Files or Photos

sections.pen_label: Test the pen: turn it on and write your name here

sections.label: Start here
steps: Download from Etsy in a web browser (the Etsy app cannot download files). Open the PDF in Goodnotes with Share, then Open in Goodnotes, or in Notability, Noteshelf, Samsung Notes or Xodo.
Go to the Setup check page and tap the buttons. If they jump, you are ready. If not, the fix is on that page.
Open Week 1, write this Monday's date, then open today's page and plan. Bought mid-week? Start on today and leave the days before it blank. Week 2 follows, then Week 3, for 52 weeks.
Pen off to tap, on to write
Links work in read or view mode. In Goodnotes, tap the pen icon off to follow a link and on again to write. To type, use your app's text tool.
sections.months_label: Months: tap the month you are in and write its dates
sections.tip: Weeks run 1 to 52 from the week you start, whatever the month. Weeks on the top bar lists all 52. Skipped a week? Leave it blank and carry on with this week.

sections.label: Lists
sections.kicker: Keep it all in one place

build_notes: Undated mode with calendar free_weeks: weeks 1 to 52 are not filed under months (Weeks page at anchor weeks), day arrows cross week edges. eink_format is used only as a layout switch (week_layout rows, custom Setup check fix list); no grayscale, no vector rules, default gutter.
